blurb: A wrong-length key slipped past the one copy endpoint its siblings already guarded, leaving billed files no client could decrypt. Found on a live server, filed with its fix.
A streaming command that hit the open-file limit silently killed the agent's shell. Traced the swallowed error and fixed the spawn.
After a terminal resize, next dev kept printing server error code frames at its startup width, so they wrapped or were cut short. Now the CLI sends the server each new width.
Electron apps in a non-ASCII folder failed to load on Linux unless the locale was UTF-8, because the archive path went through a locale conversion. Now it keeps the raw bytes.
